Lemma
[Mayer--Vietoris rank inequality]

Source: petersen:page-0488, petersen:page-0489, petersen:page-0490 1. ch12:12.5.3Let $B_i^j$, $i=1,\dots ,m$, $j=0,\dots ,n+1$, be bounded open subsets of an $n$-manifold $M$ with $\overline{B_i^j}\subset B_i^{j+1}$. Then \[ \mathrm{rank}_*\Big(\bigcup _iB_i^0\subset \bigcup _iB_i^{n+1}\Big) \le \sum _{l=0}^{n}\sum _{i_0<\cdots <i_l} \mathrm{rank}_*\Big(\bigcap _{s=0}^lB_{i_s}^0\subset \bigcap _{s=0}^lB_{i_s}^{n+1-l}\Big). \]
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch12-mayer-vietoris-rank \sketch Use the double complex whose $q$-column is the singular chain complex of $q+1$-fold intersections, with vertical boundary $\partial $ and alternating Mayer–Vietoris differential $\bar\partial $. Its total homology agrees with the homology of the union. For a finite-dimensional space of total cycles representing the relevant classes, filter by the first nonzero column. At filtration step $l$, the quotient maps into the relative homology of $l+1$-fold intersections between levels $l$ and $l+1$. Thus

\[ \dim (Z_k^l/Z_k^{l+1})\le \sum _{i_0<\cdots <i_{k-l}} \operatorname {rank}_*\left(\bigcap _{s=0}^{k-l} B_{i_s}^{l}\subset \bigcap _{s=0}^{k-l} B_{i_s}^{l+1}\right). \]

The last filtration term dies in the larger union. Summing over $l$ and degrees $k\le n$ gives the displayed Mayer–Vietoris rank inequality.

□
